methods.nursery_transplant: Raise seedlings in a nursery and transplant them to the field.
methods.drill: Sow seed in rows with a seed drill or behind the plough.
methods.dibbling: Sow seeds by hand (dibbling) on ridges or flat beds at the spacing below.
methods.setts: Plant healthy, disease-free cane pieces (setts) with 2–3 buds in furrows.

irrigation.rice: Keep a shallow layer of standing water (about 2–5 cm) from transplanting until grain filling, and drain the field 7–10 days before harvest.
irrigation.wheat: Irrigate at crown-root initiation (about 3 weeks after sowing) and again at tillering, flowering and grain filling.
irrigation.maize: Irrigate at critical stages: knee-high, tasseling/silking and grain filling. Avoid waterlogging.
irrigation.soybean: Usually rainfed. Give protective irrigation during flowering and pod filling if there is a dry spell.
irrigation.cotton: Water is most critical at flowering and boll development. Avoid waterlogging; furrow or drip irrigation is efficient.
irrigation.sugarcane: Needs frequent irrigation, especially at germination and in the grand-growth stage. Reduce in winter and stop before harvest.
irrigation.chickpea: Grows mostly on stored soil moisture. If water is available, one or two irrigations before flowering and at pod development help; avoid excess water.
irrigation.groundnut: Irrigate at flowering, pegging and pod development. Avoid waterlogging.
irrigation.onion: Give light, frequent irrigation and keep soil evenly moist. Stop irrigation 10–15 days before harvest.
irrigation.tomato: Keep soil evenly moist (drip with mulch works well) and avoid water stress at flowering and fruit set.

harvest.rice: Harvest when about 80–85% of the grains in the panicle turn straw-coloured.
harvest.wheat: Harvest when the grains are hard and the straw turns golden-yellow.
harvest.maize: Harvest when the husks dry and the kernels are hard.
harvest.soybean: Harvest when the leaves have dropped and the pods are dry and yellow-brown.
harvest.cotton: Pick fully opened bolls in two or three pickings.
harvest.sugarcane: Harvest at maturity once the leaves yellow; check with your local sugar mill for the best time.
harvest.chickpea: Harvest when the leaves and pods turn yellow-brown and dry.
harvest.groundnut: Harvest when the leaves yellow and the inside of the pod shell shows dark markings.
harvest.onion: Harvest when about half of the tops have fallen over, then cure the bulbs in shade.
harvest.tomato: Pick fruit at the stage that suits your market distance, from mature green to fully red.

timing.n_three_splits: Apply all phosphorus and potassium at sowing or transplanting. Split nitrogen into three doses: at planting, during active vegetative growth, and at the next critical stage.
timing.n_two_splits: Apply all phosphorus and potassium and half of the nitrogen at sowing; apply the remaining nitrogen after the first irrigation (about 3 weeks after sowing).
timing.all_basal: Apply the whole dose as a basal application at sowing.
timing.splits: Apply phosphorus and part of the nitrogen and potassium before planting; give the rest in two or three split doses during growth.
timing.follow_local: Fertilizer needs vary widely by state, variety and irrigation. Follow your state agricultural university's recommendation and a soil test.

extra.k_if_deficient: Apply potassium only if a soil test shows a deficiency.
extra.gypsum_flowering: Apply gypsum (about 500 kg/ha) around flowering for better pod filling.
